# Re-entry Navigation Case Plan: Keyzelle Thomas

**Staff Contact:** Turn90 Re-entry Team  
**LS/CMI Score:** 17/43 (Medium Risk/Need)  
**Primary Focus:** Employment & Dynamic Cognitive Restructuring  

---

## 1. Dynamic Focus Areas & Clinical Targets
- **Primary Target: School / Work (EE Subscore 5/9):** Zero payroll months in the past year; Associate's degree holder with strong technical ability but disrupted employment history. Goal is placement in a prosocial, fair-chance, first-shift role.
- **Secondary Target: Procriminal Attitude (PA Subscore 2/4):** Addressing 'technical legal violation' justifications for drug distribution under acute financial stress.
- **Excluded Target: Criminal History (Static 6/8):** Static factor; excluded from dynamic intervention target selection.

---

## 2. Clinical & Facilitation Strategies
1. **Modeling Neutrality (Standard 1.5):** Avoid debating past judicial fairness or the legitimacy of drug laws. Ask curiosity-based reflective questions: *'How does carrying that view of the law impact your ability to maintain your freedom and coach your team?'*
2. **Managing Resistance & Buy-In (Standard 3.2):** Explicitly link every program benchmark to his paternal anchor and youth coaching identity. Frame wage stability as the protection shield for his family.
3. **Medical Bottleneck Triage:** Prioritize medical clearance for suspected sleep apnea before placing him in high-vigilance or machinery operations to prevent workplace termination.

---

## 3. Stabilization Steps
- **Housing:** Enroll in transitional housing placement ahead of 11/17/2026 discharge.
- **SCDMV Debt:** Partner with Midlands Fatherhood Coalition to resolve $300+ tag debt.
- **Health Care:** Schedule primary care / sleep apnea assessment via Cooperative Health.

# My Fresh Start Action & Resource Guide: Keyzelle Thomas

**Welcome Keyzelle!**  
Your associate's degree, strong technical background, dedication as a father, and passion as a youth football coach demonstrate your leadership capacity. This guide outlines local Columbia resources and employment opportunities designed to help you secure housing, protect your driver's license, manage your health, and launch a rewarding career.

---

  *Services:* Emergency & program housing, case management, daily meals.  
  *Links:* [Visit Website](https://transitionssc.org) | [Directions](https://maps.google.com/?q=2025+Main+St+Columbia+SC+29201)

---

## Local Fair-Chance Employment Matches

Participant: Keyzelle L. C. Thomas | Assessment Portfolio Document: CASE BRIEF | Page 1
CASE MANAGEMENT REENTRY BRIEF
PARTICIPANT: KEYZELLE THOMAS (DOB: 12/04/1987)
Assessment Date: August 27, 2026 | Staff Contact: Turn 90 Reentry Team
1. RISK PROFILE & CRIMINOGENIC NEED DOMAINS
Keyzelle Thomas's standardized LS/CMI assessment calculates a Section 1 Total Score of 17 / 43, placing him in the
Medium Risk/Need category. This indicates that while he possesses deeply ingrained historical risks, he exhibits
exceptional cognitive, prosocial, and familial protective shields that can be leveraged during his transition. Per strict case
instructions, his high Criminal History score (6/8) is excluded from target selections, establishing the following prioritized
criminogenic need focus areas:
• Primary Domain: School / Work (EE Subscore: 5/9): Keyzelle completed high school and holds an Associate's-level
Technical College credential from Midlands Technical College. However, due to chronic incarcerations, he has worked 0
payroll months in the last year, lacks a continuous 12-month employment history, and is currently unemployed. Securing a
stable, living-wage job with an employer vetted for prosocial conditions is his primary step toward baseline stabilization.
• Secondary Domain: Procriminal Attitude / Orientation (PA Subscore: 2/4): Keyzelle exhibits active cognitive
justifications for his offending, stating that his crimes were 'only crimes because they are illegal.' He is highly resentful of
past judicial sentences, denying their fairness. Case managers must target this neutralizing cognitive distortion to prevent
relapse.
• Tertiary Domain: Substance Abuse (ADP Subscore: 1/8): While currently in stable recovery with no active drug use in
over 16 months, his historical addiction to marijuana is the direct driver of his property crime and drug distribution career.
Ongoing recovery maintenance is required to prevent relapse under occupational or financial stress.
2. BEHAVIORAL INDICATORS & THINKING PATTERNS
Observation and interview records indicate a complex, highly cooperative profile. Keyzelle is polite, patient, and
respect-oriented, but exhibits key thinking patterns and physical barriers that staff must actively navigate:
• Justifying / Minimizing (Attitude Distortion): Keyzelle neutralizes guilt by categorizing drug distribution strictly as a
technical legal violation rather than a moral wrong. This pattern allows him to bypass legal boundaries when facing acute
financial stress.
• 'Trouble is Expected' Mindset: He views justice involvement as a natural consequence of doing crime rather than a
lifestyle failure: 'No, because if you're doing crime, you expect to get in trouble.' This matter-of-fact perspective indicates a
normalized criminal identity that requires cognitive-behavioral restructuring.
• Avoidance & High Cooperative Asset: When disrespected or challenged, Keyzelle's default coping strategy is prosocial:
'I try to leave from that situation.' He got along exceptionally well with past bosses and coworkers, showing high
team-oriented potential.
• Sleep Apnea / Obesity Barrier (Physical Coping): Keyzelle was terminated from two past jobs because he 'couldn't stay
awake on the job because I was very obese.' This severe physical health barrier directly affects his workplace attendance
and performance, requiring medical evaluation.
3. JUSTICE TRAJECTORY & PATTERN OVER TIME
Keyzelle's justice involvement began at age 17 with his first arrest. In adulthood, he developed a property-offending and
drug-distribution pattern, culminating in a federal conviction for Conspiracy to Distribute Marijuana. His community
supervision is marked by chronic instability, having his supervised release revoked twice (for 41 days and 21 months) due to
technical and arrest violations. In total, he has spent approximately 3 years of his adult life incarcerated and is finishing his
current sentence. The cycle we are interrupting is chronic supervision failure and vocational collapse driven by active
marijuana distribution and untreated physical health issues.

-- 1 of 2 --

Participant: Keyzelle L. C. Thomas | Assessment Portfolio Document: CASE BRIEF | Page 2
4. ACUTE / EMERGENCY NEEDS
At intake, Keyzelle presents a severe housing crisis. He is currently completing his sentence in the federal halfway house,
but upon his scheduled release on November 17, 2026, he is considered homeless with no permanent housing arranged.
He also faces a severe financial crisis, receiving 0 active income, relying entirely on food stamps, and worrying about
outstanding debts.
5. STRUCTURAL STABILITY FACTORS
• Housing Transience: High. Currently at the halfway house, facing homelessness upon release. Requires immediate
transitional housing placement.
• Transportation Barrier: Low. Possesses a valid driver's license and a personal car, but owes the driver's license division
$300-something dollars in unpaid tag debt, risking sudden suspension.
• Financial Liabilities: High. In debt to Chime/Cash App, owes child support, and faces creditor calls. Budget compliance
is high when he has funds, but he currently has 0 income.
• Maternal/Paternal Anchor: Excellent (Family Strength). Shares an outstanding, close relationship with his highly
supportive parents.
• Prosocial Peer Shield: High (Companions Strength). No close friends are involved in crime. He has successfully
insulated himself from negative peers, and has high leadership potential as a youth football coach.
6. LEGAL & PLACEMENT CONSTRAINTS
Keyzelle is completing his sentence under active federal halfway house placement, with home confinement eligibility on
September 14, 2026, and an 'all-the-way-out' date on November 17, 2026. He has no pending charges. He has a history of
high tension with past supervision agents ('very unreasonable and she wasn't fair'), requiring careful, structured case
manager advocacy.
7. RESPONSIVITY & ENGAGEMENT PROFILE
• Leverage Father / Coach Identity: Keyzelle's primary emotional motivator is his children and his identity as a youth
sports coach. Staff should actively leverage this strength, treating him as a positive leader and role model to reinforce his
prosocial self-esteem.
• Address Health & Sleep Apnea: Reentry plans must prioritize pairing him with medical clinics to evaluate his severe
obesity and suspected sleep apnea. Resolving his physical fatigue is a critical bottleneck to preventing employment
termination.
• Cognitive Restructuring for Justification: Utilize Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) to challenge his technical
rationalizations of crime, helping him connect drug distribution to the real-world harm inflicted on his children, family, and
community.
• License & Financial Stabilization: Case management must assist him in paying off his $300+ driver's license division
debt to prevent suspension, and set up a manageable repayment plan with child support enforcement once employed.

-- 2 of 2 --
